**1. Outside view.**
The series has been running in a 50–56 band since early July, after a June bump (64–69, WWDC-driven) faded. Week-to-week moves are typically 1–5 points, with occasional 10–15 point jumps at event-driven inflections. A naive extrapolation of the last three readings (56, 56, 52) gives ~53–55, essentially flat. The scale anchor (100) is the September 2025 event week, which remains inside the trailing 12-month window, so no renormalization shock is expected this release.

**2. Inside view.**
The target week is Aug 23–29 — the classic window in which Apple issues press invitations for its early-September iPhone event (2025: invites Aug 26; 2024: Aug 26; 2023: Aug 29). That reliably produces a first step up in "iPhone" search interest before the much larger event-week spike. Historically late-August weeks sit maybe 10–25% above the mid-summer trough on this normalization. Worth roughly +4 to +8 points over the ~53 baseline. Rumor-cycle leaks (colors, pricing, Air/Fold variants) add a point or two of drift, already partly visible in the Aug 1/Aug 8 readings of 56. Nothing in the world-events digest is relevant to iPhone search demand. Sampling noise on a completed week is ±1–2 points.

**3. Pre-mortem.**
Most likely way I'm wrong: the invite lands on Sept 1–2 rather than Aug 25–26 (event date drifting later, or a Tuesday-after-Labor-Day announcement), so Aug 23–29 stays a quiet pre-event week and prints 52–55, i.e., I'd be 5 points high. The symmetric failure — an unusually early invite plus a leak storm pushing 68–72 — is less likely but possible. Correcting for the more probable downside, I shade my central estimate toward the low 58s rather than the low 60s and widen the spread.

**4. Calibrate.**
Typical inter-release move is 2–5 points, but this specific week sits on a seasonal inflection whose timing is uncertain by roughly a week, which fattens both tails. An sd of ~5.5 puts one-sigma at roughly 53–64, covering both "flat pre-event week" and "invite-week bump," which feels right for two-thirds coverage.
